subject: castle-walls-v3
label: Castle curtain wall, towers and gate — the EXISTING kit's look, at the new size
notes: V2 WAS REJECTED FOR ART DIRECTION, NOT FOR TECHNIQUE. The projection fix worked (lean went from -96.5px to 0.0px) and the sizes were right. But I specced 'cool blue-grey stone, no honey tone' — taken from the cliff-separation logic — and threw away the art style Raheem had already approved. He was blunt and correct: 'Why are you trying to make a Malfoy grey castle? The other one has gold trim, grey bricks, white bricks. It looks good with the theme we're building. What you built is depressing.'

THE RULE THIS ESTABLISHES: when approved art already exists, MEASURE IT AND MATCH IT. Do not derive a look from first principles alongside art the client has already signed off. The only thing wrong with the old kit was its SIZE.

MEASURED PALETTE of the approved pieces (gatewatch tower, corner-outer, gate arch) — sampled, not remembered: honey-gold sandstone rgb(214,184,145) / (220,196,147) / (224,188,137) at R-B +69 to +88; cream highlight rgb(204,188,162) at R-B +42; cool VIOLET-grey brick rgb(119,109,117) / (113,105,107) / (89,78,87) at R-B ~0 to +6. Note the greys are slightly violet, not blue. Honey trim is 25-35% of the visible surface — it is a major element, not an accent.

SEPARATION FROM THE CLIFF NOW COMES FROM SILHOUETTE, NOT HUE. The v2 plan used cool grey to stop a 288px wall merging with a 256px cliff into one 544px slab. That still matters, but it is bought with the DEAD-STRAIGHT CRENELLATED TOP against the cliff's irregular organic lip, plus the wall's flat even lighting against the cliff's darkening base. Both are stated positively in every prompt below. Warm honey trim actually helps here — the cliff is honey-and-grey natural rock, the wall is honey-and-grey CUT masonry, and the eye reads 'quarried from this hill', which is better world-building than a colour clash.

PALETTE IS FORCED AFTERWARDS, NOT HOPED FOR. Every piece gets lib/ramp_transfer.py against castle-tower-gatewatch-healthy.png. That is the CORRECT use of the tool — carved castle stone onto carved castle stone, same material family. It is the opposite of the logged pillar error, where carved stone was matched onto NATURAL cliff rock and vanished into it. Never run it across material families.

SIZES CARRY OVER FROM V2 UNCHANGED — they were right. Hero 100px, ground tiles 32px, cliff face 256px, cliff stair 288px. Wall 288px (2.88x hero, 32px above the cliff, shares a datum with the stair). Tower 384px (3.84x, a clear 96px / 33% above the wall). Gate 320px.

TWO V2 PIECES FAILED ON CONTENT AND ARE RE-SPECCED: the buttress came back as a slender ornamental spire instead of a wall support, and both corners came back as standalone square turrets rather than a wall turning a corner. Wording below names the wall running INTO the corner explicitly.

ONE ENDPOINT PER STRUCTURAL FAMILY. All /create-image-pixen, view 'side'. /create-tiles-pro with tile_feature 'building' is what produced the raking projection in the first place and is not used here.

SEAM-AUTHORED, NOT MIRRORED. Coursed masonry is directional; mirroring is what turned the stair into a symmetric arch. Even coursing, no off-centre features, asymmetric detail lives in the discrete buttress module.
